messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high GPU pool pressure detected for pool 'g4-hot-us-west-2' — sustained queue >90% for 8m and elevated 429s across gateway. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/inc/3745612345

oncall-bot: Paging @sam (primary). Runbook: gpu-capacity-exhaustion -> follow hotpool surge checklist.

sam: I'm taking this. quick status please — are customers impacted or internal-only degradation?

maya: Multiple hosted API customers seeing intermittent 429s and failed requests. Not limited to enterprise orgs; standard tier also affected. P95 latency increased ~1.4s. Tokenbucket reject metric aligns with queue spikes.

raj: Autoscaler shows repeated scale attempts being throttled by provider quota and a controller backoff loop. Also seeing controller rate limiter producing 429s to internal orchestrator API which slowed scale actions. snippet:

```
2026-04-02T21:02:11Z kube-orch WARN: 429 Too Many Requests - retrying
2026-04-02T21:02:48Z autoscaler ERROR: attempted scale-out -> aborted (provider_quota_limit)
2026-04-02T21:03:05Z pool-controller INFO: active-queue=1395 tokenbucket_rejects=+1860
```

leo: Found a templating bug in the Helm chart that rendered hotpath burst as an empty string when an override was present during yesterday's mass deploy. Effective burst fell to near-zero for hotpath tier. Diff of rendered config:

```yaml
# rendered tokenbucket (partial)
hotpath:
  rate: 400
  burst: ""  # templating bug -> treated as 0
enterprise:
  rate: 1200
  burst: 6000
```

ashley: Ops confirmed the mass deploy included a chart override that inadvertently triggered the bug. That explains sudden token starvation even as GPUs are saturated.

sam: Plan: 1) patch the Helm template immediately to default burst to previous safe value if empty, 2) restore hotpath burst to 1200, 3) request emergency quota increase + temporary preemption of low-priority pools, 4) apply traffic-shedding rules to non-SLA customers. Who does which?

maya: I'll apply the chart patch and the revert of the rendered config. Doing dry-run then apply.

raj: I'm on the infra request. Opening an urgent ticket with cloud provider for +10 GPUs in us-west-2 and asking infra to preempt from low-priority pools if needed.

leo: Creating a quick admission controller rule to reject helm rollouts that produce empty burst values; pushing as emergency hotfix. PR: https://git.redwood/helm/hotfix/3723.

ops-bot: helm apply started: tokenbucket-revert -> prod-us-west-2 (change set cs-90011).

ashley: Applying traffic-shedding: routing policy to downgrade standard-tier non-SLA calls to 'gpt-econ-v1' for 12m window. ops-bot queued change. CS notified of possible degraded quality.

ops-bot: routing change applied: downgrade standard-tier -> gpt-econ-v1. Auto-rollback 12m.

raj: infra responded: can provision +8 GPUs, estimated join time ~4m; preemption accepted for 4 low-priority nodes. Requesting expedited join.

maya: tokenbucket controller logs after apply:

```
2026-04-02T21:07:52Z tokenbucket-controller INFO: hotpath burst restored 0 -> 1200
2026-04-02T21:08:05Z tokenbucket-controller INFO: token pool refill stabilized; rejects trending down
```

maya: 429s dropping from 32% -> 10% in last 2m. queue 1395 -> 620. Good trend but still elevated.

sam: raj, any update on nodes?

raj: Nodes started joining. cloud provision logs show 6/8 nodes ready. kube join in progress. If remaining two fail, we'll fall back to cross-region spillover for standard tier.

leo: autoscaler log shows leader election recovered; however we hit an internal retry budget that delayed scale by ~80s. Adding an alert for controller API 429s.

ops-bot: infra update: 6 nodes joined, pool capacity increased. replicas adjusted.

maya: after nodes added and tokenburst restored + routing shim, queue down to 180, 429s ~1.4%, tail latency improving. Tokenbucket_rejects near zero.

sam: initial RCA (partial): root causes were 1) Helm templating bug rendered hotpath burst empty during mass deploy, starving short bursts and causing rapid tokenbucket rejects; 2) autoscaler reaction delayed by controller API 429/backoff and leader election hiccup; 3) cloud region quota limited immediate scale-out; 4) no safety checks in deploy pipeline to block empty burst values. Mitigations: chart patch + revert, emergency infra capacity, traffic-shedding, preemption of low-priority nodes.

ashley: Follow-ups recommended: add unit test to Helm charts to assert burst > 0 for hotpath, add CI gate to block mass rollouts if any tier burst changed by >50%, add autoscaler-slowdown alert (controller 429s or leader-election >30s), and add pre-warm policy to request nodes when queue >500 for 90s. Also add a post-deploy canary for ratepolicy changes.

raj: I'll own infra action items and update quota playbook. I'll also coordinate with cloud provider for longer-term quota increases for hotpool.

maya: Filing postmortem draft: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/3745612345-gpu-burst-templating-bug (assign sam, maya, raj). Adding timeline, graphs, and customer hit list.

sam: thanks. Julia/Tasha please prepare a short customer-facing status if we need it; otherwise hold until 15m stable.

tasha: noted. drafting standby message for status.redwood.ai.

sam: leaving maya as incident owner for watch window 30m. If recurrence, escalate to SRE management.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated: mitigations applied, metrics stable. Continue monitoring for 30m then close. :white_check_mark:
